newsitem.title: USA: Buenos Aires bank settles U.S. civil case.
newsitem.headline: Buenos Aires bank settles U.S. civil case.

text.p: Federal prosecutors said Monday that Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires has paid more than $1.2 million to settle civil claims arising from the handling of loans guaranteed by the Small Business Administration.

The settlement marks the end of a probe of the Argentinian bank that began when the government learned of allegations that a bank loan officer was demanding and accepting illegal gratuities in connection with loans guaranteed by the SBA, said Mary Jo White, U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York.
The SBA is a federal agency that offers low-interest-rate loans to small businesses.

The officer, Luis Carrizo, was convicted earlier this year in Manhattan federal court and sentenced to 18 months in prison. White said the bank cooperated with the U.S. government in its investigation of Carrizo.

The case involves charges that the bank improperly administered the guaranteed loan by taking compensating balances from borrowers to cover the non-guaranteed part of the loans. The bank also allegedly failed to disburse the loan proceeds properly, and failed to share certain loan repayments with the SBA.
Under the settlement, the bank has reimbursed SBA for the amounts the agency had paid it earlier on six loan guarantees, as well as multiple damages and penalties.
